Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award:-
1. By way of present judgment/award, I shall dispose of the claim petition filed by the
petitioners under section 166(4) of M. V. Act 1988 for grant of compensation.

2. The petitioners have filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking
compensation to the tune of Rs. 50,00,000/- alongwith interest @18% p.a. from the
date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization with cost for the fatal
injuries sustained by their deceased son Macp No. 557/19; Fir No. 271/18 Dod:
11.08.2023 namely Suraj, aged about 16 years who died in Motor Vehicular
Accident which occurred on 29.06.2018 at about 4:45 pm at Road from Banauli to
Baraut, Uttar Pradesh, involving vehicle bearing registration no. Up-17D-
7498 (offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 in a rash and
negligent manner.

3. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on
29.06.2018, Suraj (deceased herein) and Sh. Ravinder were going to their house.

At about 4:45 Pm,
when they reached Road from Banauli to Baraut, offending vehicle which was being driven by its
driver/respondent no.1 at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit against
Suraj and Ravinder with a great force, as a result of which, Suraj fell down on the road and sustained
serious post traumatic injuries and underwent series of diagnostic tests including Ct Scan and
X-rays.

After prolonged treatment with intermittent hospitalization and Opd visit, victim Suraj
succumbed to his injuries and unfortunately expired on 14.10.2018. injuries.

It is categorically
averred that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending
vehicle bearing registration no. Up-17D-7498 being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1 herein).

17. The initial burden lies upon petitioners to prove that Suraj (deceased) died due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident in question.
The petitioners are required to discharge the said burden on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.

18. The postmortem report Ex. PW2/4 in one column shows the manner of death of injured Suraj (now deceased) to be natural but in another column the cause of death shows to be due to severe head injury, extreme emaciation, severe anemia, infected bed sore with septic shock.
The same further shows that the cause of death could not be ascertained, viscera preserved & being sent to FSL Agra/Lucknow for further examination.
However, there is no FSL report filed on record.
It is apparent on record that the deceased was under treatment of PGIMER, Chandigarh at the time of his death.

The injured Suraj (now deceased) was brought to Advance Trauma Centre Emergency in critical state with unstable vital signs on 14.10.2018 and died on the same day at about 11:43 pm.
The initial medical detailed diagnosis and treatment soon after the accident on 29.06.2018 is duly proved on record vide testimony of PW1.

It is further evident from the treatment record and testimony of PW2 who clearly deposed that the MLC file of injured Suraj (now deceased) was made at the time of his initial admission on 03.07.2018 and thereafter, probably the patient was brought in emergency on 14.10.2018 at 11.30 PM and declared 'dead' at 11.43 PM and as such, in the absence of MLC file, the concerned doctor might have written as "natural death".

While deciding claim petition under M.V Act, the Claims Tribunal is guided by the principles of justice, equity and good conscience and realistic, pragmatic and liberal approach is appropriate.

23. In the light of aforesaid discussion and in view of the unrebutted testimony of PW2 Dr. Kumar Saurabh and medical treatment record proved by PW1 as Ex. PW1/6(colly), the entire history of medical treatment record from the date of accident on 29.06.2018, admission of then injured Suraj at PGIMER, Chandigarh on 03.07.2018 till 10.07.2018, the entire OPD treatment undergone by the victim from the date of accident till the date of his unfortunate demise on 14.10.2018, clearly demonstrate the miserable condition of the victim since the date of accident owing to the injuries sustained by him in the accident particularly in parietal region.

The evidence on record duly establishes that the injured remained in pitiable condition throughout the days of survival post the date of accident for a duration of almost 3  months when he eventually succumbed to his post traumatic condition on 14.10.2018.
The death summary of the patient(now deceased) merely mentioning as "Natural" apparently was noted for want of knowledge of medical history by the Certifying Doctor.

This fact is clearly reflected from the death summary prepared at PGIMER,
Chandigarh as Ex.PW2/4, wherein the cause of death was opined as "severe head injury MACP No.
557/19; FIR No. 271/18 DOD: 11.08.2023 with extreme emaciation with severe anemia with infected bed sore and septic shock".

There is nothing left to imagination or speculation to arrive at determinate conclusion that the deceased Suraj expired owing to the injuries sustained in the road accident in question and thereafter his LRs are entitled to press the present claim petition as a death case.

Counsel for petitioners has heavily relied upon the criminal case record (which is part of criminal case record) in order to bring home his point that the accident in question has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

He further argued that respondent no. 1 Sh. Subhash was also chargesheeted by police for offences punishable U/s 279/337/338 IPC, which clearly establishes that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
25.

Instead of referring to a series of decisions on the point in issue, it may be noted that it is well settled legal position as laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court as well as by various High Courts in plethora of judgments delivered from time to time that in claim petitions preferred U/s 166/140 M.V Act, the claimants have to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of alleged offending vehicles by its drivers.
